facts.claim: Slack's hosted MCP server is at https://mcp.slack.com/mcp over streamable HTTP; SSE is not supported.
facts.evidence: Docs give the URL and 'We do not support SSE-based connections or Dynamic Client Registration at this time.'; the protected-resource document is served on the same host.

facts.claim: No dynamic client registration: the client is a Slack app you create (confidential OAuth with client id and secret).
facts.evidence: Docs: confidential OAuth with the app's client_id and client_secret; the authorization-server document has no registration_endpoint and only client_secret_post.

facts.claim: Authorization runs at https://slack.com/oauth/v2_user/authorize with tokens from https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.user.access; the issuer is https://mcp.slack.com.
facts.evidence: Discovery: issuer https://mcp.slack.com, authorization_endpoint slack.com/oauth/v2_user/authorize, token_endpoint slack.com/api/oauth.v2.user.access; docs page lists the same endpoints.

facts.claim: Per-tool user scopes: search:read.public (search), channels:read (list channels), channels:history (read channel), users:read (user info), chat:write (send or schedule a message); offline_access is not among the supported scopes.
facts.evidence: Docs scope table; the protected-resource document scopes_supported lists these and no offline_access.

facts.claim: Only directory-published or internal apps may use MCP; workspace admins approve and manage MCP client integrations.
facts.evidence: 'Only directory-published apps or internal apps may use MCP.'

facts.claim: Documented writes: send message, schedule message, create conversation, add reaction, create/update canvas, upload file, create/update lists; no delete tool is documented.
facts.evidence: Tool list by category on the docs page.

facts.claim: Slack treats a localhost redirect (for example http://localhost:8080/auth) as a desktop redirect once the app has opted into PKCE; otherwise redirect URLs must be https.
facts.evidence: Localhost redirects are 'treated as desktop redirects if the app has opted into PKCE'; installing-with-oauth: 'The redirect_uri must use HTTPS.' Not yet tried against a live app.

facts.claim: The MCP authorization server advertises only client_secret_post for the token endpoint, so the client secret is sent.
facts.evidence: token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported [client_secret_post]. Slack's PKCE page says a PKCE app is a public client and the exchange should not include client_secret: the two disagree. Not tried.

facts.claim: Slack's protected-resource metadata names https://mcp.slack.com (the origin) for the /mcp endpoint; lotr 0.5.0 accepts a same-origin, whole-segment path prefix and sends that identifier as resource.
facts.evidence: Document: resource https://mcp.slack.com; lotr SPEC 0.5.0 discovery rule names this Slack case.

facts.claim: PKCE is enabled in app settings (OAuth & Permissions; Published App Settings for directory apps) or by pkce_enabled: true under oauth_config; it is one-way; PKCE apps get 30-day refresh tokens and desktop redirects cannot request bot scopes. PKCE is generally available since March 2026.
facts.evidence: PKCE page; Slack changelog 2026-03-30 announces PKCE general availability in app settings.

choices.because: Slack's official MCP is hosted and needs your own app (no DCR).

choices.decision: narrow default scopes: public search and read, users, chat:write
choices.because: Narrowest set that covers search, reading and posting; private and DM scopes are opt-in.

choices.decision: sending is write, delete/remove/archive/kick is consent
choices.because: Owner rule: posting a message is call_write, deleting is consent.
Slack does not support that scope; asking for it would be an invalid scope.

choices.decision: redirect localhost:8977 with PKCE on, client secret sent
choices.because: Slack accepts http://localhost only as a PKCE desktop redirect; the MCP authorization server lists only client_secret_post.

open: Not yet tried against a live Slack app: the localhost redirect with PKCE on, and whether oauth.v2.user.access accepts (or refuses) client_secret from a PKCE-enabled public client. If the exchange fails with the secret, set client_secret_required false.
Slack's PKCE page does not say whether the redirect port must match exactly; the template registers a fixed port (8977) to be safe.
The PKCE page does not mention the MCP user flow (oauth.v2.user.access); that the desktop-redirect rule applies to it is assumed.
Exact tool names are not on Slack's page (third-party guides show send_message / search_public, with or without a slack_ prefix); the policy globs are written to match either.
Whether Slack's token endpoint returns a refresh token depends on the app's token-rotation setting; not verified.
